waveName: Wave 2 – Workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours & preview, photo intake, design system

package.title: Robust photo loading, finger-friendly cropping, safe photo replacement
package.goal: Huge or broken photos neither crash nor fail silently. Cropping works with a finger. Replacing a photo does not silently mismatch the old mosaic or old face regions. Custom palette codes stay stable across recomputes. Degenerate cut cells in old projects are repaired when the project loads.
steps:
imagePrep:
- readImageSize(blob): HTMLImageElement natural size, which already respects EXIF.
- loadWorkingBitmap(blob, maxPx=16e6): one uniform scale, orientation 'from-image', resizeQuality 'high'. Fall back to a full decode if the aspect ratio drifts by more than 0.5 % or the call throws.
- photoErrorKey(file, err) returns 'photo.err.heic', 'photo.err.decode' or 'photo.err.save'.

useProject:
- Use loadWorkingBitmap at both decode sites and keep sourceSize.
- In compute(): when the crop at the capped resolution has fewer source pixels than the target working size, decode a temporary full-resolution bitmap from image.original, render, and close it in finally.
- Custom mode: pass code: p.code into FixedColor.
- On load, call repairDegenerateCells (from wave 1). If it repairs any cells, expose repairedCells and schedule a mosaic save.

setPhoto(blob, name, {clearRegions}) sets imageRev (from wave 1) and clears regions when asked.
StepPhoto: when replacing a photo on a project that is computed or has regions, show a dialog:
- 'Neues Projekt mit diesem Foto anlegen' (recommended): createProject, then navigate.
- 'Foto in diesem Projekt ersetzen': regions are cleared by default; a checkbox keeps them.
- 'Abbrechen'.

StepPhoto:
- onFile is async with try/catch, a loading state and an error paragraph (role=alert). The previous photo stays when decoding fails.
- PhotoInput gets a primary?: boolean prop; 'Anderes Foto' is secondary.
- Show the original pixel size plus the working size when reduced.
- Add a dismissible tip 'Porträt? Gesicht in Schritt 6 markieren' (stored in localStorage inside try/catch).

CropEditor:
- Four corner handles, each a 44×44 transparent hit area with an 18-20 px dot, placed INSIDE the box so overflow:hidden cannot clip them.
- Resize around the opposite corner, projecting the drag onto the diagonal, with the aspect ratio fixed and clamped to the image.
- Minimum box size about 90 CSS px.
- setPointerCapture, plus pointercancel and lostpointercapture cleanup.
- A zoom slider (100-15 %) that scales around the centre.
- Readout 'Ausschnitt W×H px · ≈ N px pro Stein'.
acceptance: e2e at 390×844 with touch: dragging from 15 px inside the bottom-right corner by (-100,-100) shrinks the crop and keeps width/height equal to the layout aspect ±0.5 px. The same works from the top-left handle.
e2e: uploading an 8000×6000 JPEG shows the original size and a working size ≤16 MP, and the compute succeeds. An EXIF orientation 6 photo stays portrait with the correct corner at the top.
e2e: a corrupt file in the photo step shows the alert and keeps the previous photo.
Replacing the photo after compute opens the dialog. Choosing 'ersetzen' clears the regions and shows the stale badge.
Unit test: a custom palette with code gaps keeps its codes across two computes when run through useProject's input building. Test the helper as a pure function if needed.
package.risk: Effort M. createImageBitmap resize options behave differently in older WebViews; keep the full-decode fallback. The memory peak during the first decode remains.

findings.title: An unreadable photo (corrupt file or HEIC on desktop) does nothing: no error message, only an uncaught exception
findings.problem: Home.newProject() and useProject.setPhoto() await loadBitmap() without catching errors. If the browser cannot decode the file (corrupt JPEG, HEIC from an iPhone or some Android cameras on desktop Chrome, RAW, …), the button just re-enables or nothing happens. The user gets no feedback at all.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t11_bad_image.cjs, output t11_output.txt: 'Home upload: url = http://localhost:4173/ | visible errors = [] | uncaught = [ InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded. ]' and the same for the photo step. Code: Home.tsx:24-38 (try/finally with no catch), StepPhoto.tsx:70 (void api.setPhoto(...)), useProject.ts:186-202.

Use an error state in Home and the existing .error paragraph in StepPhoto. Check file.type/size before decoding. Do not create the project if decoding fails.

findings.title: A full-resolution photo bitmap stays in memory for the whole session: a 48 MP phone photo costs about +285 MB, a crash risk in Android WebView
findings.problem: loadBitmap (imagePrep.ts:10-16) decodes the original at full resolution, and useProject keeps that ImageBitmap in state for the lifetime of the project (useProject.ts:73-81, 186-197). The app never needs more than workingSize (max 6 MP, imagePrep.ts:128-133), and the crop preview is 900 px wide. ImageBitmap.close() is never called anywhere, so replaced photos are freed only when GC runs. Modern phones produce 48-200 MP photos, and the WebView renderer on mid-range Android devices is memory-limited.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/bigphoto.cjs measures the RSS of the Chromium process tree (phone emulation) when loading a photo through home-photo and then computing. 3 MP: 'chromium tree RSS 459 MB -> 520 MB (+61 MB)', peak 595 MB. 48 MP (8000x6000, .../img/photo48mp.jpg): 'RSS 461 MB -> 746 MB (+285 MB)', 'peak during compute 807 MB'. The crop canvas is only 900x675 in both cases. grep for '.close()' in src/ui and src/workers finds no bitmap close.
findings.proposal: In loadBitmap, first read the dimensions (createImageBitmap(blob) and close it, or decode the header), then decode again with { imageOrientation: 'from-image', resizeWidth/resizeHeight such that the long side is at most 4096 px, resizeQuality: 'high' }. That is enough for 6 MP working size plus crop headroom and caps memory at about 64 MB. Call prev.close() in setPhoto and in the useProject unmount cleanup. Optionally store a downscaled JPEG (long side 4096, q 0.92) next to the original and use only that in the app. Add a note in the photo step when the source was reduced.
corrected:
1. Change src/ui/project/imagePrep.ts loadBitmap so it returns `{ bitmap, srcW, srcH }` and never decodes at full size just to learn the dimensions:
   - Read the size from the header: create an object URL, load it into an `Image` and wait for `onload` (do not use `img.decode()`), take naturalWidth/naturalHeight (these already respect EXIF), then revoke the URL.
   - If srcW*srcH > MAX_PX (about 16e6, which is about 64 MB of RGBA), call `createImageBitmap(blob, { imageOrientation: 'from-image', resizeWidth: round(srcW*s), resizeHeight: round(srcH*s), resizeQuality: 'high' })` with `s = sqrt(MAX_PX/(srcW*srcH))`. Otherwise keep today's call. Keep today's code as the fallback if anything throws.
   - A limit on pixel area keeps crop room for workingSize (6 MP) and keeps panoramas usable, which a 4096 px long-side limit does not.
2. Fix src/ui/Home.tsx:29 and :44. They decode a full bitmap only to compute the aspect ratio and never release it. Use the header-only size read there, or call `b.close()` right after reading width and height. Closing alone lowered the measured load peak from about 840-880 to about 745 MB.
3. In src/ui/project/useProject.ts, release replaced or unmounted bitmaps with `useEffect(() => () => { bitmap?.close(); }, [bitmap])` instead of closing `prev` inside setPhoto. That way a pending render (StepPhoto or StepShapes) or effect cannot use a bitmap that is already closed. compute() uses the bitmap synchronously before it awaits the worker, so it is safe either way.
4. In src/ui/project/StepPhoto.tsx:104, show the original and the working size when the photo was reduced, for example "8000 × 6000 px (bearbeitet mit 4618 × 3464 px)". Add the strings in de, en and tr.
5. Expect, as measured: about 110 MB less memory at rest and at the compute peak for a 48 MP photo. The load peak stays high because Chromium still decodes at full size before resizing. Photos at or below 16 MP, which includes the default 12 MP phone photo, are unchanged.
6. Add an e2e check: upload an 8000x6000 JPEG and assert that the displayed working size is at most MAX_PX. Upload an image with EXIF orientation 6 and assert that it stays portrait with the correct corner on top (resize applies to the oriented dimensions in Chromium 153). Rate impact 2-3, effort S.

Use a capped bitmap for working in the project, but compute from the full image when needed. The mosaic result stays identical to today, so geometry, counts and cut dimensions are untouched.

1. imagePrep.ts: add loadWorkingBitmap(blob, maxSide = 4096). It returns { bmp, origW, origH, reduced }.
   - Decode once with { imageOrientation: 'from-image' } and read origW and origH.
   - If max(origW, origH) > maxSide:
     - Close that bitmap.
     - Decode again with resizeWidth and resizeHeight set from ONE uniform scale factor, plus resizeQuality 'high'.
     - Check that |bmp.width/bmp.height - origW/origH| < 0.5%. If the check fails, or the call throws, fall back to the full decode (protection for old WebViews).
   - This order measured the lowest peak.
   - Keep loadBitmap for the full-resolution path.

2. useProject.ts: use the new loader at both decode sites, :79 (opening a project) and :188 (new photo). Store origW and origH in state.
   - effectiveCrop and the aspect calculation can keep using the capped bitmap, because both only need the aspect ratio.
   - In compute():
     - Compute rw and rh from origW and origH via rotatedSize, and compute ws with workingSize exactly as today (sourcePx = crop.w*rw*crop.h*rh).
     - If the crop at capped resolution has fewer pixels than ws.w*ws.h, decode a temporary full bitmap from image.original. Otherwise use the capped bitmap.
     - Call renderCropped, then close the temporary bitmap in a finally block.
   - The working image then has the same pixel count as today. Compare the hashes of the old and new raw.data for the four sample projects and a 48 MP photo.

3. Home.tsx:29 and :44: call b.close() right after reading the aspect ratio. These are full-resolution decodes that are never released today.

4. Release bitmaps through the React lifecycle, not inside setPhoto. In useProject, add `useEffect(() => () => { bitmap?.close(); }, [bitmap]);`.
   - Cleanups run after child effects such as StepPhoto's 180 ms timer have been cleared, which avoids drawImage on a detached bitmap.
   - With StrictMode, the double-invoke at mount happens while bitmap is still null, so it is harmless.

5. StepPhoto.tsx:104: show the original size, plus a note when the image was reduced, e.g. "8000 × 6000 px (for editing reduced to 4096 × 3072; the calculation uses full resolution)". Add the string to i18n de/en/tr.

6. Do not claim it fixes the load-time memory peak: createImageBitmap's resize still decodes at full resolution. If the peak itself turns out to crash on a device, a follow-up would be to decode in a worker or in strips. That should be measured on a real Android device before it is promised.

7. Tests:
   - e2e: upload the 48 MP JPEG and assert that the crop canvas and the mosaic-canvas appear.
   - unit or e2e: an EXIF orientation 6 photo keeps portrait orientation after the capped decode.
   - Assert the identical working-image size before and after the change for a 1000x750 cm project with a 10% crop.

findings.title: Full-resolution photos are kept decoded and never released (ImageBitmap.close() is never called), and PDF object URLs leak
findings.problem: Each Workspace mount decodes the original photo at full resolution (a 48 MP phone photo is about 190 MB of RGBA). Home.newProject decodes it once more only to read the aspect ratio. Nothing calls bitmap.close(): not on photo replacement, not on unmount, not in Home. Memory stays high after leaving the project, which risks renderer or WebView crashes on Android phones (which in turn hit the unsaved-debounce problem). StepPdf also creates an object URL for every generated PDF and never revokes it, so each regeneration keeps the previous multi-MB blob alive.
findings.evidence: Measurement: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t13_bitmap_memory.cjs with big48mp.jpg (8000×6000), output t13_output.txt: Chromium RSS 'baseline 450' → 'after opening 779' → 880–1127 MB while reopening 6 times → 'after leaving project, 5 s idle 1108' MB (not released). Code: grep finds no '.close()' in src; imagePrep.ts:10-16 (full-res createImageBitmap), Home.tsx:29 and 44, useProject.ts:79/188-192, StepPdf.tsx:71 (createObjectURL with no revoke; downloadBlob in components.tsx:162-169 does revoke).
findings.proposal: On import, downscale to a working copy (long edge ≤ 4096 px, enough for 40M positions) using createImageBitmap(blob, {resizeWidth, resizeQuality:'high'}). Store it as the 'working' image and keep the original blob only for export. Call bmp.close() in Home after reading width/height, in setPhoto before replacing, and in a useProject unmount cleanup. In StepPdf, revoke the previous result.url before setResult and in a useEffect cleanup.
corrected:
Low priority (impact about 2, effort S). Change only where memory is freed; image quality stays the same.

1. Keep two images in useProject.ts:
   - A preview bitmap for the screens, decoded with createImageBitmap(blob, {imageOrientation:'from-image', resizeWidth/resizeHeight so the long edge is at most 4096, resizeQuality:'high'}). StepPhoto, CropEditor, StepShapes, StepGeometry and originalPreview use it, and crop coordinates stay normalized.
   - The real photo size, kept in state as `sourceSize`. Use it for the "W x H px" label in StepPhoto.tsx:104 and for the aspect-ratio math.
2. Decode the full-resolution photo only during compute. In runCompute (useProject.ts:277-290), decode image.original, pass it to renderCropped, then call close() in a finally block right after canvasToRaw. Compute input is then exactly what it is today.
3. Call close() on the old bitmap in three places: in setPhoto before setBitmap, in a useEffect cleanup keyed on the bitmap, and in the load effect when `alive` is false.
4. In Home.tsx:29 and 44, call close() right after reading width and height.
5. In StepPdf, keep the URL in a ref. Revoke the previous URL before setResult({url}), and revoke the current one in an unmount cleanup.

Check the result with mem3.cjs: at most one bitmap alive at any time, and renderer memory down when a project is reopened.

Part A (effort S, do it now; compute results stay identical):
1. **Home.tsx:29-30 and 44-45:** close the bitmap right after reading the aspect:
   `const b = await loadBitmap(photo); aspect = b.width / b.height; b.close();`
2. **useProject.ts:79-80:** `if (alive) setBitmap(bmp); else bmp.close();`
3. **useProject.ts:** release the old bitmap only after React has committed the new one, never inside `setPhoto` before `setBitmap`:
   ```
   const liveBmp = useRef<ImageBitmap|null>(null);
   useEffect(() => { const old = liveBmp.current; liveBmp.current = bitmap; if (old && old !== bitmap) old.close(); }, [bitmap]);
   useEffect(() => () => { liveBmp.current?.close(); liveBmp.current = null; }, []);
   ```
   This is safe under StrictMode because the bitmap is still null when StrictMode does its test unmount.
4. **StepPdf `generate`:** call `api.originalPreview(1800)` and encode it before the first await, or wrap it in try/catch. Then leaving mid-generation can never draw a closed bitmap.
5. **StepPdf object URL:**
   - Create it only when `!isNative()`.
   - Keep it in `urlRef`, and revoke the previous one when a new generation starts.
   - Add `useEffect(() => () => { if (urlRef.current) URL.revokeObjectURL(urlRef.current); }, [])` above the early `if (!c || !G) return`.
6. **Regression check:** add a Playwright case that opens a project with a large photo, goes to Projects, reopens it, and checks that the photo step still shows the real pixel size and that Compute and PDF work.

Part B (effort M, optional; keep two versions of the image instead of shrinking the one used for the calculation):
1. On load, decode a preview bitmap with `createImageBitmap(blob, {imageOrientation:'from-image', resizeWidth, resizeHeight, resizeQuality:'high'})`, long edge at most 3072-4096.
2. Use it for StepPhoto, CropEditor, StepShapes and originalPreview, and for `effectiveCrop`. The crop is stored as fractions of the image, so it is the same at any size.
3. Store the original width and height when the photo is imported, and show those as the "px" size.
4. In `compute()`, decode the full-resolution original from `api.image.original` on demand, then run `renderCropped` and `canvasToRaw`, then close it right away. The working image stays exactly as today (up to 6 MP of the crop), so tight crops such as faces keep full colour detail.
5. Do not feed a 4096 copy into `workingSize` as the compute source.

findings.title: Crop editor is not usable by finger: its only resize handle is clipped to 13x13 px, and by default the crop always touches that corner
findings.problem: CropEditor has one 20x20 px resize handle positioned at right/bottom -9px (styles.css:762-773). The parent .crop-holder has overflow:hidden (styles.css:~428), so when the crop box reaches the image corner only a 13x13 px quarter circle is visible and hittable. That is the default: setPhoto adapts the project height to the photo's aspect ratio (useProject.ts:197), so the default crop covers the whole image. A finger landing 12 px inside the corner hits .crop-box (move) instead, and since the box is already full size nothing happens. The crop cannot be made smaller on a phone. There is no pinch-resize, no other corner handle, and no pointercancel handling.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/crop.cjs (output .../out/crop.txt): 'holder {x:25,y:330.7,w:340,h:425}', 'crop-box' identical to the holder, 'handle hit area visible inside holder: 13.0 x 13.0 css px', 'element 12px inside bottom-right corner: crop-box', and 'crop-box after finger drag from 12px inside corner' is unchanged at 340x425. Screenshots: .../shots/crop-corner.png (quarter handle) and .../shots/m-phone-step-photo.png.
findings.proposal: In CropEditor.tsx, render four corner handles (nw/ne/sw/se). Each has a 44x44 transparent hit area with a 20 px visual dot placed inside the crop box (e.g. right: 0; bottom: 0; transform: none), so they are never clipped. Alternatively, give the holder padding/overflow:visible. Resize with the fixed aspect ratio from the opposite corner. Support a two-finger pinch on .crop-box (scale around the midpoint while keeping the aspect ratio, clamped to the image). Register 'pointercancel' alongside 'pointerup'. Offer a 'Zoom/Ausschnitt' slider as a non-gesture fallback. Show the crop size in px and the resulting resolution per stone.
corrected:
Fix the hit target first. This is effort S.
1. In styles.css, give .crop-handle a hit area of at least 44x44 css px with a 20 px visible dot. Either make the element 44x44 and transparent with a ::after dot, or keep the visual size and add an invisible ::before with inset:-12px.
2. Keep the hit area inside the clipped region. Either:
   - give .crop-holder about 22 px of padding with the image canvas inset, and keep the handle centered on the corner, or
   - place the handle inside the box (right:0; bottom:0; no negative offset).
   The current overflow:hidden on .crop-holder (styles.css:738) only exists to round the canvas corners. If you prefer, move the border-radius onto the canvas and set .crop-holder to overflow:visible. Then make sure no ancestor clips it, and give the page enough side padding (about 22 px) so the 44 px target stays fully on screen.
3. Render four corner handles (nw/ne/sw/se) in CropEditor.tsx. Each resizes around the opposite corner, which stays fixed. Keep the aspect ratio and clamp to the image. Derive the new width from max(|dx|, |dy|*aspect) projected along the drag diagonal, not from dx alone as at CropEditor.tsx:37. Otherwise a mostly vertical finger drag does nothing.
4. Set the minimum crop size in css px of the displayed holder, at least about 2x the hit area (roughly 90 px), not 20 source px. Handles must not cover the whole box, so moving it stays possible.
5. Register 'pointercancel' next to 'pointerup' in CropEditor.tsx:51 to remove the listeners. Optionally use setPointerCapture on the pointerdown target.

Optional, effort M:
- A two-finger pinch on .crop-box that scales around the midpoint with the fixed aspect ratio, clamped to the image.
- A 'Ausschnitt/Zoom' range slider under the editor as a fallback that needs no gestures.
- Display the crop size in source px plus px per stone. Compute it only from the real crop and the layout, so nothing is invented.

Add an e2e check like crop-verify.cjs: a touch drag that starts 15 px inside the bottom-right corner must shrink the crop.

1) src/ui/project/CropEditor.tsx: render four handles (nw, ne, sw, se) as children of .crop-box. Each handle is a transparent 44x44 hit area with a ::after visual dot of 18-20 px. Place them INSIDE the box so `overflow:hidden` on .crop-holder can never clip them, e.g. se: right:0; bottom:0; and transform-origin so the dot sits on the corner line. If the crop box renders smaller than about 110 px, show only the se handle so handles do not overlap.
   - startDrag(e, mode) takes the corner. The opposite corner stays fixed in pixel space.
   - New width in px = clamp(start width ± dx·rw, 20, max width allowed by the image edges in that direction).
   - h = w/aspect, then apply the same `sc = min(1, maxW/wPx, maxH/hPx)` scaling as now, so the aspect stays exact and the box stays inside [0,1].
   - Recompute x/y from the fixed corner.
   - Use `el.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` (or keep the window listeners) and remove them on BOTH 'pointerup' and 'pointercancel'.
2) StepPhoto.tsx (under the CropEditor): add a Slider "Ausschnitt / Zoom" from 100% down to about 15% that scales the current crop around its centre. Use the same math as fitCrop with areaPx multiplied by s², clamped to the image, aspect unchanged. It works with any finger, a keyboard, or a mouse, and needs no new gesture code. Also show a line, computed rather than estimated: "Ausschnitt: W × H px · ≈ N px pro Stein" (crop px / layout.cols and crop px / layout.rows).
3) Optional, lower priority (M): two-finger pinch on .crop-box. Track two pointerIds, scale = current distance / start distance, apply the same centre-scaling + clamp function as the slider.
4) styles.css: delete right/bottom:-9px from .crop-handle and add the 44 px hit-area + ::after dot rules. Keep `touch-action:none`.
5) e2e/run-e2e.cjs: add a hasTouch 390x844 case. Open sample-portrait → step-photo, drag with CDP touch from 15 px inside the bottom-right corner by -100/-100, and assert that the .crop-box width shrank and width/height still equals layout aspect ±0.5 px. Repeat from the top-left handle.
These changes stay inside the crop editor and cannot affect layout, stone counts or cut dimensions.

findings.title: Replacing the photo after a compute is not detected as a change, so the PDF shows the new photo next to the old mosaic
findings.problem: computeKey contains layout, shapes, palette settings, adjust and regions, but nothing that identifies the image. setPhoto only resets crop, rotation and flip. If those were already at their defaults, the key is unchanged, so no stale badge appears anywhere. The old mosaic stays and is presented as current. The PDF takes its 'Originalfoto' from the CURRENT bitmap (api.originalPreview), so the plan pairs a city photo with a portrait mosaic. Face and detail regions from the old photo are also kept for the new one. The PDF step has no stale warning at all, even for normal setting changes.

findings.title: Own palette ('Eigene Palette') loses unused colours and renumbers its codes on every Berechnen
findings.problem: In 'custom' mode (and 'materials' mode) computeMosaic drops every palette entry that no stone uses, sorts the rest by L* and renumbers them 1..n. useProject then saves res.palette as the project palette and uses rec.palette as the custom palette for the next run. So the user's own colours and numbers (requirement 7: '01=Weiss') are lost for good after one compute: a colour that is unused once can never come back, and a code can point to a different colour after a recompute. Separately, nextCode() = max(code)+1 gives a deleted colour's code to the next new colour, so sheets printed earlier (requirement 10: print sections separately) no longer match the legend.

findings.title: Manual triangle edit (DIAG) is not validated: empty or too-small stones, Infinity in stats and CSV

On narrow edge cells this creates triangles below the minimum size. When the joint is wider than about twice the cell's narrow side, clipping returns empty polygons that are still counted as 2 stones. analyzeCut on an empty polygon reports fits=true, needsCut=true, w/h=-Infinity, and the CSV prints Infinity coordinates.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
